speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether there are measures implemented to protect Singapore's carded athletes from the misuse of drugs; and (b) if so, what are they.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether the Government or National Sports Associations (NSAs) have any programmes to educate national and elite athletes about the dangers and pitfalls of using recreational drugs and performance-enhancing drugs; and (b) whether the Government or NSAs have any programmes that regularly test their national and elite athletes for recreational drug use and performance-enhancing drug use.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: SportSG works with ADS and the broader sporting fraternity to ensure that sport in Singapore is free of doping and that our national athletes compete fairly and safely, and that they can be upheld as role models for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: At the national level, Singapore has a clear, well-established policy on drugs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In the context of sport, Singapore has a framework of rules and standards to keep sports in Singapore free of doping, including the use of both recreational drugs and performance-enhancing drugs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It aims to equip our national athletes with the information, tools and values for them to exercise sound judgement and choices when it comes to the use of drugs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: There are two key strategies in which this is implemented: (a) through education and prevention; and (b) through detection and deterrence.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: One, education is a key preventive measure to discourage intentional or inadvertent doping, and this is done through various platforms.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First, all National Sports Associations (NSAs) are expected to inform and educate their athletes and athlete support personnel on issues concerning sports doping under the framework.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Second, ADS works with NSAs to plan, implement and monitor education programmes for athletes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These comprise regular updates on issues, such as the currency of prohibited substances and methods, the health consequences of doping, and the rights and responsibilities of athletes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: ADS also reminds NSAs and their athletes on their anti-doping obligations at all pre-Major Games briefings.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To prevent inadvertent doping, ADS provides the "Check Drugs" function on its website to enable athletes and support personnel to check on the prohibited status of a particular drug or substance.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For medications not on the database, athletes can and should check with a sports physician or with ADS directly.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Two, on the detection and deterrence front, ADS oversees a robust doping testing regime.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First, ADS develops and regularly reviews a test distribution plan for athletes, with higher testing frequencies for athletes assessed to be at higher risk of doping.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Several factors are considered in determining the risk level of doping, such as the athlete's performance and the type of sports.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: ADS' testing regime covers both in-competition and out-of-competition tests.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Second, ADS also relies on intelligence, such as whistle-blowing sources, to identify and investigate allegations of drug abuse, including following up to conduct tests on alleged offenders.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These sanctions are made public to send a deterrent signal to others.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For instance, SportSG could suspend the spexScholarship or other support offered to a carded athlete.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The NSA may also suspend training support for the athlete or their selection for competitions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) or the Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) may also, separately, suspend the selection of the athlete for any Major Games for the appropriate period.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Notwithstanding the range of sanctions that can be taken, it is also important to consider a rehabilitative approach to help the athlete not to offend again.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The sporting community will work with the athletes to provide counselling and rehabilitative support they may need.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Government and the local sporting fraternity looks upon the misuse of drugs as a serious matter.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: SportSG, ADS and the fraternity will continue to work together to underscore the importance of complying with Singapore's laws on drugs and anti-doping rules at all times.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Just one supplementary question, Mr Speaker, on the aspect of education.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I agree with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary that this is key as a preventive measure.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given that many of our national athletes or perhaps, many of our athletes, get competitive much earlier on – in school, perhaps – would ADS and SportSG consider working with the relevant authorities or the relevant Government agencies to go further upstream in terms of providing education to our younger competitive athletes who would, obviously, hopefully, become national athletes, seeing as to how the youths could be a bit more impressionable, to have these education programmes further upstream such that they are aware of the pitfalls of using recreational and performance-enhancing drugs in their athletic endeavours?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I will make a broad point about what Mr Darryl David has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The pursuit of excellence in sport is not just limited to the technical aspects of it.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think this is consistent across sports, cultures and jurisdictions, if I may put it that way.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.
